q: An e-auction of scrap has been finalised and the lots have been sold. The earnest money deposited by the bidders who remained unsuccessful in the auction is:

options.A: Refunded to them after finalisation of the auction
options.B: Forfeited to the Railway in all cases
options.C: Adjusted compulsorily against their future purchases
options.D: Credited to the Stock Adjustment Account

e: Earnest money is taken only to secure the bids; once the e-auction is finalised, the earnest money of unsuccessful bidders is refunded to them.

q: On completion of a work, serviceable stores released from the work are returned to the stores depot and taken into stock. The credit given to the work for the stores so returned is at:

options.A: The price at which the stores were originally issued to the work
options.B: The assessed value of the stores returned
options.C: The current market price of new stores
options.D: A nominal value of one rupee per item

e: Serviceable stores returned to depot on completion of a work are taken into stock at their assessed value, and the work is credited with that assessed value, not the original issue price.

q: Twelve wagons loaded with stores are detained at a depot for 3 days beyond the free time allowed for unloading. Demurrage is payable at Rs 950 per wagon per day. The total demurrage payable is:
e: Total demurrage = 12 wagons x 3 days x Rs 950 = Rs 34,200.

q: Midway through a stores contract, the Railway requires an additional quantity of the same item. By invoking the option clause in the purchase order, the Railway may:

options.A: Transfer the order to another firm
options.B: Change the specification of the material
options.C: Cancel the order without notice
options.D: Order the additional quantity on the same terms and conditions during the currency of the contract

e: The option clause in a purchase order permits the Railway to order an additional quantity of the same item on the same terms and conditions during the currency of the contract.

q: An item held in a depot has not been used for the last 24 months, and it is also not expected to be used during the next 24 months. The item is treated as:

options.A: Dead surplus stores
options.C: Obsolete stores
options.D: Insurance spares

e: Per Para 118 of the Stores Code Vol. I, dead surplus stores are items not issued for 24 months and not likely to be utilised on any railway within the next two years.

q: The average value of stock held by a railway is Rs 3.4 crore. If the inventory carrying cost is estimated at 11 per cent per annum of the average stock value, the annual inventory carrying cost is:
e: Annual inventory carrying cost = 11 per cent of Rs 3.4 crore = Rs 37,40,000.

q: A supplier fails to fulfil his stores contract and does not supply the stores satisfactorily in accordance with its terms. The Security Deposit furnished by him under the contract is:

options.A: Refunded to him in full at once
options.C: Adjusted against his earnest money in another tender
options.D: Credited to the Stock Adjustment Account

e: The Security Deposit secures due fulfilment of the contract; on the supplier's failure to supply satisfactorily in accordance with its terms, the deposit is liable to be forfeited under the IRS Conditions of Contract.

q: After purchasing a scrap lot in an e-auction, a purchaser complains that the material is not in the condition he had expected. Scrap lots in an e-auction are sold on the basis that:

options.A: The Railway guarantees the condition of the material
options.B: The purchaser may return the material within a month
options.C: The Railway will repair the material before delivery
options.D: The material is sold 'as is where is', the purchaser taking it in its existing condition and position

e: Scrap lots in an e-auction are sold on an as is where is basis; the purchaser takes the material in its existing condition and position and the Railway gives no guarantee of condition.

q: During stock verification, a shortage of 29 units of an item is found. The book rate of the item is Rs 540 per unit. The value of the shortage to be accounted for is:
e: Value of shortage = 29 x 540 = Rs 15,660, shortages found on stock verification being accounted for at the book rate of the item.

q: A stores tender has been finalised and accepted. The Earnest Money Deposit of the tenderers who remained unsuccessful in the tender is:

options.A: Refunded to them after the tender has been finalised and accepted
options.B: Forfeited to the Railway in all cases
options.C: Adjusted compulsorily against all their future tenders
options.D: Credited to the Stock Adjustment Account

e: Once the tender is finalised and accepted, the Earnest Money Deposit of the unsuccessful tenderers is refunded to them; it is forfeited only on default of the successful tenderer.

q: The programme of stock verification of a stores depot is so arranged that:

options.A: All items are verified on one single day of the year
options.B: Only items costing above Rs 1 lakh are verified
options.C: Verification is carried out once in five years
options.D: Every item is physically verified at least once in a year

e: The stock verification programme is so arranged that every item in a depot is physically verified at least once in a year, as required by the Stores Code.

q: A depot holds 1,320 units of an item. The book rate of the item is revised from Rs 57 to Rs 49 per unit. The decrease in the value of the stock in hand, which is adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account, is:
e: Decrease in stock value = 1320 x (57 - 49) = 1320 x 8 = Rs 10,560, adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account on revision of the book rate.

q: The storekeeper of a ward in a stores depot is responsible, in respect of the stores in his charge, for:

options.A: Fixing the purchase price of the stores
options.C: The safe custody of the stores and the correctness of the balances held by him
options.D: Granting tenders to firms

e: The storekeeper of a ward is responsible for the safe custody of the stores in his charge and for the correctness of the balances held by him.

q: A depot officer proposes to insure the railway stores held in his depot with a commercial insurer against fire and theft. As a rule of financial propriety, Government property, including railway stores held in depots, is:

options.A: Not insured commercially, Government bearing its own risk of loss
options.B: Insured with a commercial insurer against all risks
options.C: Insured only against the risk of theft
options.D: Insured by the depot officer at his personal cost

e: As a rule of financial propriety, Government bears its own risk of loss and Government property, including railway stores in depots, is not insured commercially.

q: The opening debit balance under Purchase Suspense of a railway is Rs 11 lakh. During the month, stores bills amounting to Rs 36 lakh are paid and material worth Rs 41 lakh is received at the depots and linked with the bills. The closing balance under Purchase Suspense is:

options.A: Debit Rs 5 lakh
options.C: Debit Rs 7 lakh
options.D: Credit Rs 6 lakh

e: Closing Purchase Suspense = opening debit 11 + bills paid 36 - material received and linked 41 = Rs 6 lakh debit.

q: While fixing the Average Annual Consumption (AAC) of a stock item, the figure is arrived at keeping in view:

options.A: The consumption of the item in the last month only
options.B: The production capacity of the supplier of the item
options.C: The past consumption trend of the item and the anticipated future requirements and programmes
options.D: The book rate of the item in the Priced Stores Ledger

e: The Average Annual Consumption is fixed from the past consumption trend of the item together with anticipated future requirements and the programmes of the consuming departments.

q: Stores are issued from a depot to a consuming department. The head of account to which the value of the issue is to be debited is indicated on the:

options.A: Bin Card
options.C: Issue Note
options.D: Tender Notice

e: Stores are issued on an Issue Note, which indicates the head of account to which the value of the issue is to be debited.

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 66 lakh and its Turnover Ratio is 0.22. The total issues of stores during the year are:

options.A: Rs 2.5 crore
options.C: Rs 4 crore
options.D: Rs 3 crore

e: On the Railways the Turnover Ratio is the ratio of the closing balance of stores to the total issues, so total issues = 66 / 0.22 = Rs 300 lakh = Rs 3 crore.

q: Dead surplus stores have been circulated to other depots and railways, but no depot or railway requires them. Such stores are finally disposed of:

options.A: By free distribution among the depot staff
options.B: By return to the original suppliers at the purchase price
options.C: By transfer to the Works Department without any accountal
options.D: After survey/condemnation, by sale as scrap through e-auction

e: Dead surplus stores not required by any depot or railway are, after survey and condemnation, disposed of by sale as scrap through e-auction.

q: During stock verification of an item, the physical stock is found to be in excess of the book balance. For recording this difference, the stock verifier prepares:

options.A: No document, since a stock sheet is prepared only for a shortage
options.B: A stock sheet, a stock sheet being prepared for an excess as also for a shortage
options.C: A narrative report only, without any stock sheet
options.D: A fresh bin card for the item

e: A stock sheet is prepared for every difference found on verification, whether the physical stock is in excess of or short of the book balance.

q: Scrap having a book value of Rs 92,000 is sold by e-auction for Rs 79,500. The difference of Rs 12,500 between the book value and the sale value is:

options.A: Credited to the Stock Adjustment Account
options.C: Debited to the Stock Adjustment Account
options.D: Debited to Purchase Suspense

e: Scrap sold for Rs 79,500 against a book value of Rs 92,000 results in a loss of Rs 12,500, which is debited to the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: In fixing the stock levels of an item, the minimum level is set at:

options.A: The maximum quantity that may be held at any time
options.B: The quantity consumed in one year
options.C: The quantity ordered in one purchase order
options.D: The safety (buffer) stock level, below which the balance should not ordinarily be allowed to fall

e: The minimum level of an item is its safety or buffer stock, the level below which the balance should not ordinarily be allowed to fall.

q: The inventory carrying cost borne by a railway on its stores is usually reckoned as:

options.A: A percentage of the average value of the inventory held, per annum
options.B: A fixed amount per depot, irrespective of the stock held
options.C: A charge per item, irrespective of its value
options.D: A percentage of the salary bill of the stores department

e: Inventory carrying cost, covering interest on capital, storage, handling and deterioration, is reckoned as a percentage per annum of the average value of the inventory held.

q: A stores depot issues 260 units of an item, whose book rate is Rs 140 per unit, to an outside party. Departmental charges are leviable at 12.5 per cent of the book value. The total amount recoverable from the party is:
e: Book value = 260 x 140 = Rs 36,400; departmental charges at 12.5 per cent = Rs 4,550; total recoverable = 36,400 + 4,550 = Rs 40,950.

q: In an ABC analysis of the stores of a depot, a small group of items is found to account for the bulk of the annual consumption value of the depot. These items are placed in:

options.A: 'A' category
options.C: 'C' category
options.D: 'Z' category of XYZ analysis

e: In ABC analysis items are ranked by annual consumption value; the small group of items accounting for the bulk of that value forms the A category and gets the closest control.

q: At the end of a month, the Purchase Suspense account of a railway shows a credit balance. On examination, a credit balance under Purchase Suspense indicates that:

options.A: Bills have been paid but the material has not been received
options.B: Material has been received at the depots but the suppliers' bills have not yet been paid
options.C: Stores have been issued to workshops in excess of their demand
options.D: Stores losses have been written off after stock verification

e: A credit balance under Purchase Suspense means material has been received at the depots and taken to stock, but the suppliers' bills for it have not yet been paid.

q: Tenders for a stores item are to be opened in the purchase office. A tenderer asks to be present at the opening. Stores tenders are opened:

options.A: At the appointed date and time, in the presence of such tenderers or their authorised representatives as wish to attend
options.B: Only after the tender has been finally accepted
options.C: Secretly by the purchase clerk in his own room
options.D: At any time convenient to the depot storekeeper

e: Stores tenders are opened at the appointed date and time in the presence of such tenderers or their authorised representatives as wish to attend.

q: A depot requires a standard stores item and the purchase office takes up its procurement. As a rule, stores required by the Railways are ordinarily procured to:

options.A: Specifications framed separately by each depot for itself
options.C: The specification of whichever firm supplied the item last time
options.D: Indian Railway Standard (IRS) specifications or RDSO specifications and drawings

e: Stores are ordinarily procured to Indian Railway Standard (IRS) specifications or RDSO specifications and drawings, so that a uniform standard is maintained across the Railways.

q: A purchase officer is drafting the specification for a stores item to be tendered and proposes to write it around the product of one particular manufacturer. Specifications prescribed for the procurement of stores are required to be:

options.A: Generic, functional and broad-based, so as not to restrict competition
options.B: Specific to a particular brand or manufacturer
options.C: Drawn up so as to suit a particular firm
options.D: Copied invariably from the specification of the last purchase

e: Specifications for procurement must be generic, functional and broad-based so as to permit fair competition, in keeping with the GFR principle that specifications should not be restrictive or brand-specific.

q: A successful tenderer asks why he is required to furnish a Security Deposit when his tender has already been accepted. The Security Deposit in a stores contract is taken primarily to:

options.A: Earn interest for the Railway on the amount deposited
options.B: Meet the cost of inspection of the stores supplied
options.C: Secure due fulfilment of the contract by the supplier
options.D: Pay the charges for advertising the tender

e: The Security Deposit is taken to secure due fulfilment of the contract by the supplier and is liable to forfeiture on his default.

q: A stores purchase is of small value and falls well within the limits laid down in the delegation of powers. Such a low-value purchase may be accepted:

options.A: Only by a Tender Committee of three members in every case
options.B: Directly by the competent stores officer, without reference to a Tender Committee
options.C: Only after obtaining the approval of the Railway Board
options.D: By the depot storekeeper at his own discretion, whatever the value

e: A low-value purchase within the limits of the delegation of powers may be accepted directly by the competent stores officer without reference to a Tender Committee.

q: An indent for stores is put up to Finance for vetting, but there is no provision of funds in the Stores Budget for the purchase proposed. The correct position is that:

options.A: The purchase can be sanctioned first and the provision of funds arranged afterwards in every case
options.B: Stores are ordinarily purchased only against provision of funds in the Stores Budget, the availability of funds being checked at the stage of vetting of the indent
options.C: Funds are never required for the purchase of stores
options.D: The indentor may arrange the funds from the sale of scrap in his depot

e: Stores are ordinarily purchased only against provision of funds in the Stores Budget, and availability of funds is checked at the stage of Finance vetting of the indent.

q: A trainee in a purchase office is shown a purchase order placed on a supplier and asks what particulars such an order ordinarily carries. A purchase order for stores ordinarily specifies:

options.A: Only the total value of the order
options.B: Only the name of the supplier and the description of the item
options.C: The names of the other tenderers who had quoted for the item
options.D: The description and PL number of the stores, the quantity and rate, the consignee depot and the delivery period

e: A purchase order ordinarily specifies the description and PL number of the stores, the quantity and rate, the consignee depot and the delivery period, besides the other terms of supply.

q: In a stores depot, the custody (bin) accounts and the priced accounts of the same stores are maintained as two independent sets of records. This is done so that:

options.A: One of the two sets can be dispensed with in alternate years
options.B: Each set serves as a check on the other and the two can be agreed with each other
options.C: The depot staff need not maintain any quantity record at all
options.D: The priced accounts can simply replace the custody accounts

e: Custody (quantity) accounts and priced accounts of the same stores are maintained independently so that each set serves as a check on the other and the two can be agreed.

q: Stores have been issued from a depot to another railway and their value awaits final adjustment and recovery. Pending that adjustment, the value is accommodated in the stores accounts under the:

options.A: Purchase Suspense head
options.C: Stores Miscellaneous Suspense head
options.D: Sales Suspense head

e: The value of stores issued to another railway, pending final adjustment and recovery, is accommodated under the Stores Miscellaneous Suspense head.

q: While the Stores Budget of a railway is being framed, the 'debits' anticipated during the year are provided for. These debits represent:

options.A: The value of stores expected to be purchased and received during the year
options.B: The closing balance of stores expected at the end of the year
options.C: The value of stores expected to be issued to consuming departments
options.D: The earnest money expected to be collected from tenderers

e: In the Stores Budget, debits represent the value of stores expected to be purchased and received during the year, against which the budget provision is made.

q: A trainee asks why the Stores Budget of a railway is called a 'derived' budget. It is so described because:

options.A: It is prepared by the Railway Board directly for every railway
options.B: It carries no separate allotment of funds
options.C: It is merged with the Capital Budget of the railway
options.D: Its requirements are derived from the works and maintenance programmes of the consuming departments

e: The Stores Budget is called a derived budget because its requirements are derived from the works and maintenance programmes of the consuming departments.

q: A consuming department wishes to meet its requirement of a stock item through the integrated Material Management System. Through the user depot module (UDM) of iMMS, the department can:

options.A: Pass suppliers' bills for payment
options.B: View the stock position of items in depots and raise its demands online
options.C: Conduct e-auctions of scrap on behalf of the depots
options.D: Fix the AAC of A-category items of the depots

e: Through the User Depot Module (UDM) of iMMS, a consuming department can view the stock position of items in depots and raise its demands online.

q: Physical verification of the stores in a depot is regarded as an effective internal check on the depot's balances mainly because:

options.A: The custodian verifies his own stock and certifies it himself
options.B: The supplier of the stores verifies the stock in the depot
options.C: The balances are verified by Accounts stock verifiers who are independent of the custodian holding the stores
options.D: The purchaser of scrap verifies the stock before every auction

e: Stock verification is an effective internal check because the balances are verified by Accounts stock verifiers who are independent of the custodian holding the stores.

q: A loss of stores has been enquired into and written off under the sanction of the competent authority. The value of the loss so written off is adjusted in the stores accounts through the:

options.A: Purchase Suspense Account
options.C: Traffic Suspense Account
options.D: Stock Adjustment Account

e: The value of a stores loss written off under the sanction of the competent authority is adjusted in the stores accounts through the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: At a periodical review, a depot brings out a list of items which have shown no issues over a long period. Such 'non-moving' items are brought out in the list mainly so that:

options.A: Their book rates can be revised upward
options.B: Their continued retention can be reviewed and surplus or obsolete stock can be declared and disposed of
options.C: Fresh purchase orders can be placed for them at once
options.D: They can be transferred to the personal custody of the storekeeper

e: Non-moving items, showing no issues over a long period, are listed so that their continued retention can be reviewed and surplus or obsolete stock declared and disposed of.

q: A depot holds stores well in excess of its own foreseeable requirements, and other depots of the railway can use them. Stores so held, which are available for transfer to depots requiring them, are described as:

options.A: Dead surplus stores
options.C: Surplus stores
options.D: Insurance spares

e: Stores held in excess of a depot's own foreseeable requirements but usable by other depots are surplus stores, available for transfer to depots requiring them.

q: A purchase office is covering the requirements of its depots. The correct basis of procurement is that:

options.A: Stock items are procured against specific demands of works, and non-stock items against the AAC of the depot
options.B: Stock items are procured on the basis of depot indents linked to the AAC and coverage, while non-stock items are procured against specific demands
options.C: Both stock and non-stock items are procured only through rate contracts
options.D: Non-stock items are first taken into the priced stock of the depot and issued later as required

e: Stock items are procured on depot indents linked to the AAC and coverage, while non-stock items are procured against specific demands of works or departments.

q: Stores are drawn from a depot for the execution of a sanctioned capital work. In the accounts, the value of such stores is:

options.A: Charged to ordinary revenue expenditure
options.B: Written off as a stores loss
options.C: Held under Sales Suspense till the work is completed
options.D: Debited to the account of the capital work concerned

e: Stores drawn for a sanctioned capital work are debited to the account of that capital work, the cost forming part of the cost of the work.

q: A consuming department draws stores from a depot during a month and asks when the cost of the stores will be charged to its account. The cost of stores drawn from a depot is charged to the account of the department or work at the time of:

options.A: Issue of the stores from the depot
options.B: Purchase of the stores from the supplier
options.C: Receipt of the stores in the depot
options.D: Payment of the supplier's bill

e: The cost of stores drawn from a depot is charged to the account of the department or work at the time of issue of the stores from the depot.

q: A new folio is to be opened in the Priced Stores Ledger of a depot for an item taken into stock. In the Priced Stores Ledger, a separate folio is maintained for each stores item identified by its:

options.A: PL (Price Ledger) number
options.C: Bin number in the ward
options.D: Ward number in the depot

e: In the Priced Stores Ledger a separate folio is maintained for each stores item, identified by its PL (Price Ledger) number.

q: Stores supplied by a firm are rejected on inspection at the consignee depot. The rejected stores are lying in the depot and have to be removed. The removal is arranged:

options.A: By the Railway at its own cost in every case
options.B: By the supplier at his own cost within the period stipulated in the contract
options.C: By the depot storekeeper at his personal cost
options.D: By the next supplier who delivers stores to the depot

e: Rejected stores are to be removed by the supplier at his own cost within the period stipulated in the contract, as per the IRS Conditions of Contract.

q: Stores supplied under a contract are found defective within the warranty period and the supplier, despite notice, fails to repair or replace them. In such a case, the Railway may:

options.A: Bear the cost of repair itself without any remedy against the supplier
options.B: Drop the claim and throw away the defective stores
options.C: Arrange the repair or replacement at the supplier's risk and cost and recover the amount from his dues or security deposit
options.D: Ask the depot storekeeper to impose a fine on the supplier

e: On the supplier's failure to repair or replace defective stores within the warranty period despite notice, the Railway may arrange repair or replacement at his risk and cost and recover the amount from his dues or security deposit.

q: A purchaser of a scrap lot sold in an e-auction does not lift the material within the delivery period allowed to him, and the material continues to lie at the depot. For the period of such delay, the purchaser is liable to pay:

options.A: Demurrage charges to the wagon owner
options.B: Earnest money deposit afresh for the same lot
options.C: Price variation on the lot
options.D: Ground rent for the period for which the material remains at the depot

e: A purchaser who does not lift his scrap lot within the delivery period is liable to pay ground rent for the period the material remains at the depot.

q: A supplier contends that the liquidated damages stipulated in his stores contract are a penalty imposed on him. In law and in the contract, the liquidated damages so stipulated represent:

options.A: A genuine pre-estimate of the loss likely to be suffered by the Railway on a breach of the contract
options.B: A penalty imposed on the supplier for delayed supply
options.C: Interest payable on delayed payment of suppliers' bills
options.D: The profit element built into the supplier's rates

e: Liquidated damages are a genuine pre-estimate of the loss likely to be suffered by the Railway on breach of contract, agreed by the parties in advance, and not a penalty.

q: A stores officer explains the two basic decisions of inventory control for a stock item with the help of its Economic Order Quantity and its Re-order Level. These two together answer, respectively, the questions:

options.A: When to order and how much to order
options.B: From whom to order and at what price to order
options.C: How much to order and when to order
options.D: At what price to order and from whom to order

e: Inventory control answers two questions: how much to order, answered by the Economic Order Quantity, and when to order, answered by the Re-order Level.

q: In an inventory review of a depot, items are classified under XYZ analysis. This analysis classifies the items on the basis of:

options.A: The annual consumption value of the item
options.B: The criticality of the item for train operations
options.C: The lead time required for the item
options.D: The value of the inventory (stock) held of the item

e: XYZ analysis classifies items on the basis of the value of inventory held of each item, unlike ABC analysis which is based on annual consumption value.

q: A depot holds a safety (buffer) stock of an item below its normal working stock. The buffer stock is held primarily to guard against:

options.A: Variations in the rate of consumption and in the lead time
options.B: Pilferage of stores from the depot
options.C: Obsolescence of the item in store
options.D: A rise in the price of the item

e: Buffer (safety) stock is held primarily to absorb variations in the rate of consumption and in the lead time, so that stock-outs are avoided.

q: The inventory carrying cost per unit of an item rises, the cost of placing an order and the annual consumption remaining unchanged. Other things remaining the same, the Economic Order Quantity of the item will:

options.A: Increase
options.B: Become equal to the annual consumption
options.C: Remain unchanged
options.D: Decrease

e: EOQ varies inversely with the carrying cost per unit; when the carrying cost rises, ordering larger lots becomes costlier and the Economic Order Quantity decreases, ordering and consumption remaining unchanged.

q: An accounts clerk refers to the inventory carrying cost of stores by its other commonly used name. The inventory carrying cost of stores is also known as the:

options.A: Ordering cost
options.C: Holding cost
options.D: Landed cost

e: Inventory carrying cost is also known as holding cost, being the cost of holding stock, including interest on capital locked up, storage and deterioration.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 4,410 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 100 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 5 per unit per year. The Economic Order Quantity of the item is:

options.A: 380 units
options.C: 460 units
options.D: 420 units

e: EOQ = square root of (2 x 4410 x 100 / 5) = square root of 176,400 = 420 units.

q: A depot holds 550 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 32 per unit. A fresh receipt of 250 units is taken into stock at Rs 56 per unit. The revised book (average) rate of the item will be:

options.A: Rs 39.50 per unit
options.C: Rs 42.50 per unit
options.D: Rs 45.50 per unit

q: The AAC of an item is 8,640 units. The stock in hand is 1,080 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 360 units. The coverage available for the item is:

options.A: 1 month
options.C: 2 months
options.D: 4 months

e: Monthly consumption = 8640 / 12 = 720 units; coverage = (stock 1080 + dues 360) / 720 = 1440 / 720 = 2 months.

q: The average consumption of an item is 68 units per day, the lead time for its procurement is 11 days and the safety (buffer) stock provided for it is 212 units. The re-order level of the item is:

options.A: 748 units
options.C: 856 units
options.D: 1,064 units

e: Re-order level = average consumption x lead time + safety stock = 68 x 11 + 212 = 748 + 212 = 960 units.

q: The re-order level of an item is 1,680 units and the re-order quantity is 940 units. The minimum consumption is 52 units per week and the minimum lead time is 6 weeks. The maximum stock level of the item is:

options.A: 2,308 units
options.C: 2,412 units
options.D: 2,516 units

e: Maximum stock level = re-order level + re-order quantity - (minimum consumption x minimum lead time) = 1680 + 940 - (52 x 6) = 2620 - 312 = 2,308 units.

q: Under a stores contract, stores of the value of Rs 6,75,000 remain in arrear of supply and are supplied 4 weeks late. Liquidated damages at 0.5 per cent of the value of the stores in arrear for each week of delay amount to:
e: LD = 0.5 per cent of 6,75,000 = Rs 3,375 per week x 4 weeks = Rs 13,500, as per the liquidated damages clause of the stores contract.

q: A supplier's bill for stores amounts to Rs 6,85,000. The advance payment admissible at 98 per cent of the bill value, against the inspection certificate and despatch documents, is:
e: Advance payment at 98 per cent = 0.98 x 6,85,000 = Rs 6,71,300, payable against the inspection certificate and despatch documents.

q: The opening debit balance under Purchase Suspense of a railway is Rs 19 lakh. During the month, stores bills amounting to Rs 49 lakh are paid and material worth Rs 53 lakh is received at the depots and linked with the bills. The closing balance under Purchase Suspense is:

options.A: Debit Rs 13 lakh
options.C: Debit Rs 17 lakh
options.D: Credit Rs 15 lakh

e: Closing Purchase Suspense = opening debit 19 + bills paid 49 - material received and linked 53 = Rs 15 lakh debit.

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 84 lakh and its Turnover Ratio is 0.28. The total issues of stores during the year are:

options.A: Rs 2.5 crore
options.C: Rs 3 crore
options.D: Rs 4 crore

e: Total issues = closing balance / Turnover Ratio = 84 / 0.28 = Rs 300 lakh = Rs 3 crore, the Turnover Ratio being the ratio of closing balance to total issues.

q: A supplier fails to supply 575 units of stores contracted at Rs 92 per unit. A risk purchase of the same quantity is made at Rs 109 per unit. The extra cost recoverable from the defaulting supplier is:
e: Extra cost of risk purchase = 575 x (109 - 92) = 575 x 17 = Rs 9,775, recoverable from the defaulting supplier under the risk purchase clause.

q: Nine wagons loaded with stores are detained at a depot for 4 days beyond the free time allowed for unloading. Demurrage is payable at Rs 875 per wagon per day. The total demurrage payable is:
e: Total demurrage = 9 wagons x 4 days x Rs 875 = Rs 31,500.

q: A depot holds 2,150 units of an item. The book rate of the item is revised from Rs 73 to Rs 66 per unit. The decrease in the value of the stock in hand, which is adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account, is:
e: Decrease in stock value = 2150 x (73 - 66) = 2150 x 7 = Rs 15,050, adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account on revision of the book rate.

q: A stores depot issues 440 units of an item, whose book rate is Rs 85 per unit, to an outside party. Departmental charges are leviable at 12.5 per cent of the book value. The total amount recoverable from the party is:
e: Book value = 440 x 85 = Rs 37,400; departmental charges at 12.5 per cent = Rs 4,675; total recoverable = 37,400 + 4,675 = Rs 42,075.

q: The average value of stock held by a railway is Rs 2.85 crore. If the inventory carrying cost is estimated at 13 per cent per annum of the average stock value, the annual inventory carrying cost is:
e: Annual inventory carrying cost = 13 per cent of Rs 2.85 crore = Rs 37,05,000.

q: A purchase order is placed on a supplier for stores valued at Rs 12,60,000. The security deposit prescribed under the contract at 5 per cent of the order value works out to:
e: Security Deposit at 5 per cent of the order value = 0.05 x 12,60,000 = Rs 63,000.

q: An order banning a firm from business dealings for supply of stores is issued on one zonal railway. A purchase officer of another zonal railway asks whether the ban binds purchases on his railway as well. Banning orders issued against a firm are:

options.A: Confined to the single depot which proposed the ban
options.B: Circulated to all zonal railways and are effective across the Railways
options.C: Kept secret and not communicated to any other office
options.D: Effective for one tender only on the railway which issued them

e: Banning orders against a firm are circulated to all zonal railways and are effective across the Railways, so that no railway enters into business dealings with the banned firm during the ban period.

q: A firm which has been supplying stores to the Railways for some years asks whether its registration with the Railways, once granted, continues for all time without any review. Registration of a firm for supply of stores is:

options.A: Granted for a limited period and renewed thereafter after a review of the firm's performance
options.B: Granted once for the entire life of the firm and can never be reviewed
options.C: Granted only to firms which have never supplied stores before
options.D: Not required to be recorded in any register of firms

e: Registration of a firm for supply of stores is granted for a limited period and is renewed thereafter only after a review of the firm's performance and continued eligibility.

q: Spanners, hammers and similar tools are issued from a depot to a work gang for use on a job. Such returnable stores, issued for use against acknowledgement, are:

options.A: Consumed as soon as they are issued to the gang
options.B: Sold to the staff of the gang after use
options.C: Required to be returned to stores after use
options.D: Written off from the books at the time of issue

e: Tools and similar returnable stores are issued against acknowledgement for use on a job and must be returned to stores after use; they are not consumed or written off at issue.

q: A debit in respect of a consignment of stores has been outstanding under Purchase Suspense in the books of a railway. The balance so outstanding is finally cleared when:

options.A: The tender for the next purchase of the item is opened
options.B: The financial year comes to an end
options.C: The stock verification of the depot is completed
options.D: The material has been received and the corresponding bill has been paid and linked

e: A debit under Purchase Suspense is cleared when the material has been received and the corresponding bill has been paid and linked with the receipt.

q: A depot is repeatedly unable to supply a stores item when the consuming departments demand it, and work suffers in consequence. The losses and extra costs arising when an item is not available in stock when demanded, such as idle time of men and machines and emergency purchase at higher prices, are known as the:

options.A: Stock-out (shortage) cost of the item
options.C: Landed cost of the item
options.D: Book value of the item

e: The losses and extra costs suffered when an item is not in stock when demanded, such as idle men and machines and emergency purchase at higher prices, are the stock-out or shortage cost of the item.

q: A micro and small enterprise participating in a stores procurement asks what price it has to pay for the tender set (documents) of the tender. Under the Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises, tender sets are issued to micro and small enterprises:

options.A: At double the normal price
options.C: Free of cost
options.D: Only against their Earnest Money Deposit

e: Under the Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises, tender sets are issued free of cost to micro and small enterprises participating in procurement.

q: Wagons carrying a stores consignment to a depot are detained beyond the free time allowed for unloading because the depot could not unload them in time, and demurrage charges become payable. Such demurrage charges are:

options.A: Always borne personally by the supplier of the stores
options.B: Borne as a charge on the receiving depot/stores organisation responsible for the detention
options.C: Waived automatically in all cases for railway stores
options.D: Adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account

e: Demurrage arising from detention of wagons because the receiving depot could not unload them in time is borne as a charge on that depot or stores organisation responsible for the detention.

q: A depot official has to distinguish between two charges connected with stores consignments and material lying at a depot. Demurrage, as distinct from ground rent, is payable for:

options.A: Storage of rejected material in the depot beyond the stipulated period
options.B: Keeping purchased scrap in the depot beyond the delivery period
options.C: Occupying office accommodation in the depot premises
options.D: Detention of wagons beyond the free time allowed for unloading them

e: Demurrage is the charge for detention of wagons beyond the free time allowed for unloading, whereas ground rent is charged for material lying at a depot beyond the allowed period.

q: In stores procedure, a consuming department places a 'demand' on a stores depot for the stores it requires. As distinct from this, an 'indent' for procurement of stores against the demands received is placed by:

options.A: The depot or purchase office
options.B: The supplier on the Railway for supply of stores
options.C: The Accounts office on the depot for stock verification
options.D: The purchaser of scrap on the depot for delivery of material

e: A consuming department places a demand on the depot, while the indent for procurement of stores against the demands received is placed by the depot or purchase office.

q: The Turnover Ratio of the stores of a railway for a year works out to 0.25. This indicates that the stock held in the depots of the railway is broadly equal to:

options.A: One month's issues of stores
options.C: Three months' issues of stores
options.D: Twelve months' issues of stores

e: A Turnover Ratio of 0.25 means the closing stock equals 25 per cent of the year's issues, i.e. 0.25 x 12 = 3 months' issues of stores.

q: A supplier participating in a stores tender under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order declares that the local content of the stores offered by him is 15 per cent. Such a supplier is treated under the Order as:

options.A: A Class-I local supplier
options.C: A Class-II local supplier
options.D: A micro and small enterprise

e: Under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, a supplier with local content below 20 per cent is a non-local supplier; Class-II requires 20 to 50 per cent and Class-I 50 per cent or more, so 15 per cent is non-local.

q: Stores received in a depot are arranged and stocked in a systematic order so that any item can be located readily, identified correctly and accounted for properly. For this purpose, the stores in a depot are arranged and stocked:

options.A: In the order in which they are received in the depot
options.B: According to the names of the suppliers who supplied them
options.C: According to the dates of the purchase orders against which they were received
options.D: According to their Price Ledger (PL) numbers

e: Stores in a depot are arranged and stocked according to their Price Ledger (PL) numbers, so that any item can be located readily, identified correctly and accounted for properly.

q: A purchase order is placed on a firm against its tender, which has been duly accepted by the competent authority. In regard to the obligation of the firm, such a purchase order:

options.A: Constitutes a concluded contract binding on the supplier to supply the stores on the terms of the order
options.B: Is only an expression of intention and binds neither party
options.C: Can be withdrawn by the firm at its will at any time
options.D: Requires a separate agreement in every case before it can bind the firm

e: A purchase order placed on a firm against its duly accepted tender constitutes a concluded contract, binding the supplier to supply the stores on the terms of the order.

q: A bidder is declared the successful (highest) bidder for a scrap lot in an e-auction and proceeds to pay the sale value of the lot. The earnest money deposited by him as a bidder in the auction is:

options.A: Refunded to him immediately after the auction in all cases
options.B: Forfeited to the Railway in all cases
options.C: Adjusted towards the sale value payable by him for the lot
options.D: Credited to the Stock Adjustment Account

e: The earnest money deposited by the successful bidder in an e-auction is adjusted towards the sale value payable by him for the lot purchased.

q: Within the annual procurement target of 25 per cent from Micro and Small Enterprises under the Public Procurement Policy for such enterprises, the sub-target prescribed for MSEs owned by Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe entrepreneurs is:

options.A: 3 per cent
options.C: 7.5 per cent
options.D: 10 per cent

e: Under the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs, the annual target is 25 per cent of procurement from MSEs, within which a sub-target of 4 per cent is prescribed for MSEs owned by SC/ST entrepreneurs.

q: A stores officer is working out the inventory carrying cost of the stock held in his depot. Which of the following forms a part of the inventory carrying cost of stores?

options.A: The cost of inviting tenders for purchase of the item
options.B: The price paid to the supplier for the item
options.C: The demurrage paid for detention of wagons bringing the item
options.D: Interest on the capital locked up in the stock held

e: Inventory carrying cost includes interest on the capital locked up in the stock held, along with storage, handling and deterioration costs; tendering cost is an ordering cost, not a carrying cost.

q: Which of the following is NOT a recognised source of supply of stores under Para 201 of the Stores Code, Vol. I?

options.A: Confiscation of a defaulting contractor's material
options.C: Manufacture in railway workshops
options.D: Transfers from other stores depots and returns to stores

e: Para 201 of the Stores Code Vol. I recognises sources such as purchases through tenders and contracts, manufacture in railway workshops and transfers or returns to stores; confiscation of a defaulting contractor's material is not a recognised source of supply.

q: A Class-I local supplier in a stores tender claims purchase preference under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order. The margin of purchase preference admissible to a Class-I local supplier under the Order is:

options.A: 10 per cent
options.C: 20 per cent
options.D: 25 per cent

e: Under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, the margin of purchase preference admissible to a Class-I local supplier is 20 per cent.

q: A trainee in a stores depot asks what the Priced Stores Ledger of the depot primarily records. The Priced Stores Ledger primarily records:

options.A: Only the names of the approved suppliers of the depot
options.B: The prices (book value) at which stores transactions are accounted for
options.C: Only the physical quantities of stores, without any value
options.D: The tender notices issued by the purchase office during the year

e: The Priced Stores Ledger records the prices, i.e. the book values, at which stores receipts, issues and balances are accounted for in the depot.

q: Stores items in all the depots of the Railways are codified and identified through Price Ledger (PL) numbers under a unified Priced Vocabulary. The main purpose of such codification of stores items is to:

options.A: Fix the purchase price of each item permanently
options.B: Decide the depot in which each item will be stocked
options.C: Determine the AAC of each item of stores
options.D: Identify each item uniquely in all depots, so that the same item is not stocked under different names

e: Codification of stores items by PL numbers under the unified Priced Vocabulary identifies each item uniquely in all depots, so that the same item is not stocked under different names.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 7,225 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 100 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 8 per unit per year. The Economic Order Quantity of the item is:

options.A: 425 units
options.C: 475 units
options.D: 375 units

e: EOQ = square root of (2 x 7225 x 100 / 8) = square root of 180,625 = 425 units.

q: A depot holds 640 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 44 per unit. A fresh receipt of 360 units is taken into stock at Rs 69 per unit. The revised book (average) rate of the item will be:

options.A: Rs 49 per unit
options.C: Rs 56.50 per unit
options.D: Rs 59 per unit

q: The average consumption of an item is 92 units per day, the lead time for its procurement is 12 days and the safety (buffer) stock provided for it is 316 units. The re-order level of the item is:

options.A: 1,104 units
options.C: 1,420 units
options.D: 1,604 units

e: Re-order level = average consumption x lead time + safety stock = 92 x 12 + 316 = 1104 + 316 = 1,420 units.

q: The re-order level of an item is 1,940 units and the re-order quantity is 1,060 units. The minimum consumption is 64 units per week and the minimum lead time is 7 weeks. The maximum stock level of the item is:

options.A: 2,328 units
options.C: 2,664 units
options.D: 2,552 units

e: Maximum stock level = re-order level + re-order quantity - (minimum consumption x minimum lead time) = 1940 + 1060 - (64 x 7) = 3000 - 448 = 2,552 units.

q: Under a stores contract, stores of the value of Rs 8,40,000 remain in arrear of supply and are supplied 3 weeks late. Liquidated damages at 0.5 per cent of the value of the stores in arrear for each week of delay amount to:
e: LD = 0.5 per cent of 8,40,000 = Rs 4,200 per week x 3 weeks = Rs 12,600, as per the liquidated damages clause of the stores contract.

q: A supplier's bill for stores amounts to Rs 7,35,000. The advance payment admissible at 98 per cent of the bill value, against the inspection certificate and despatch documents, is:
e: Advance payment at 98 per cent = 0.98 x 7,35,000 = Rs 7,20,300, payable against the inspection certificate and despatch documents.

q: The opening debit balance under Purchase Suspense of a railway is Rs 23 lakh. During the month, stores bills amounting to Rs 57 lakh are paid and material worth Rs 61 lakh is received at the depots and linked with the bills. The closing balance under Purchase Suspense is:

options.A: Debit Rs 15 lakh
options.C: Debit Rs 19 lakh
options.D: Credit Rs 19 lakh

e: Closing Purchase Suspense = opening debit 23 + bills paid 57 - material received and linked 61 = Rs 19 lakh debit.

q: A supplier fails to supply 625 units of stores contracted at Rs 88 per unit. A risk purchase of the same quantity is made at Rs 106 per unit. The extra cost recoverable from the defaulting supplier is:
e: Extra cost of risk purchase = 625 x (106 - 88) = 625 x 18 = Rs 11,250, recoverable from the defaulting supplier under the risk purchase clause.

q: Seven wagons loaded with stores are detained at a depot for 6 days beyond the free time allowed for unloading. Demurrage is payable at Rs 725 per wagon per day. The total demurrage payable is:
e: Total demurrage = 7 wagons x 6 days x Rs 725 = Rs 30,450.

q: A depot holds 2,480 units of an item. The book rate of the item is revised from Rs 81 to Rs 74 per unit. The decrease in the value of the stock in hand, which is adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account, is:
e: Decrease in stock value = 2480 x (81 - 74) = 2480 x 7 = Rs 17,360, adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account on revision of the book rate.
